title: Hopf-Quotiented Quantum Shadow of the Universal Hyperbolic Base
question: What geometry survives when one point of the declared universal Poincare H4 base is encoded as a fixed-width physical density operator without identifying the hyperbolic, split-signature, and quantum metrics?

inside: a deterministic qutrit density encoding of radial depth and S3 direction
the Hopf quotient S3 to CP1 and its exact U(1) phase kernel
origin-preserving U(2) base isometries with covariant qutrit unitary transport
hyperbolic distance, tangent-matched Euclidean distance, trace distance, root fidelity, and Bures distance as separate fields
outside: identifying the Poincare metric with Bures, Fisher, Fubini-Study, or split-signature geometry
general Lorentz translations of H4 as finite-dimensional quantum gates
channel capacity, optimized coding, hardware, noise, energy, cognition, AGI, consciousness, or quantum advantage
claiming that the qutrit shadow is an injective representation of H4

definition.base_point: x in the open unit ball B4, r=||x||
definition.direction: for r>0, z=(x0+i*x1,x2+i*x3)/r in C2 with ||z||=1
definition.origin: rho_0=|flag><flag|; the arbitrary direction is multiplied by zero
definition.hopf_kernel: z and exp(i*theta)z give the same density; the corresponding H4 points are generally distinct
definition.transport: U in U(2) acts by z->Uz and rho->diag(1,U) rho diag(1,U)^dagger
definition.control: the same realified U(2) action is orthogonal on R4 and therefore preserves both H4 distance and the tangent-matched Euclidean distance

predictions.statement: Every encoded state is Hermitian, positive semidefinite, trace one, and immutable.
The qubit-block trace recovers r exactly and the hyperbolic radius is 2R*atanh(r).
Trace distance from the encoded origin is exactly r, so infinite hyperbolic depth compactifies to a finite quantum distance.
A nontrivial common Hopf phase changes the H4 point while leaving the density operator exactly invariant; the generic differential rank is three, not four.
Every declared U(2) chart preserves hyperbolic and Euclidean control distances and intertwines base transport with qutrit unitary conjugation.
A fixed qutrit dephasing channel cannot increase trace distance or decrease root fidelity.

controls.name: typed geometry separation
controls.gate: Reports retain hyperbolic, Euclidean-control, trace, fidelity, and Bures observations as separate named fields with no weighted aggregate.

controls.name: phase-aware source control
controls.gate: The source R4 vector distinguishes a nonzero Hopf phase orbit that the physical density aliases.

controls.name: origin and boundary
controls.gate: The origin is direction-independent; points on or outside the open boundary are rejected rather than clipped.

controls.name: transport covariance
controls.gate: Random frozen U(2) transports preserve source distances and quantum pair geometry to 1e-10.

controls.name: nonunitary refusal
controls.gate: A nonunitary fiber chart is rejected before transport.

controls.name: matched Euclidean ablation
controls.gate: The Euclidean control uses the existing origin-tangent-matched R4 contract and is never reported as a quantum metric.

kill_conditions: Any density is non-Hermitian, non-positive, or not trace one.
The encoded origin depends on an arbitrary direction.
A Hopf phase is reported as observable in the physical density.
A U(2) chart changes hyperbolic distance, Euclidean control distance, trace distance, or root fidelity beyond tolerance.
A dephasing control increases trace distance or decreases root fidelity beyond numerical tolerance.
Any scalar combines base distance with quantum distinguishability.
Any cognition, AGI, consciousness, capacity, hardware, or quantum-advantage interpretation is promoted.

evidence_ceiling.P: finite-dimensional algebraic and numerical invariants of this declared encoding
evidence_ceiling.S: interpretation as a quantum shadow of the HB0 base

resource_budget.expected_runtime: under five seconds for focused tests

stop_condition: Stop after the typed encoding, U(2) covariance, phase-kernel report, matched controls, bounded documentation, focused tests, full-suite regression, and evidence-envelope verification. Do not add a reservoir service, hardware emulator, or capacity experiment in this round.
